title: Single-nucleus isolation from frozen human lung tissue for single-nucleus RNA-seq
author: Nikita Joshi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zu8f6zw

steps.title: Prepare Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the following stock solutions and keep them on ice:

substeps.instruction: Prepare cOmplete stock, 10x.
Prepare Lysis buffer, 2 ml per sample.
Prepare Wash buffer, 4 ml per sample.
Prepare Resuspension buffer, 0.3 ml per sample.

steps.title: Tissue Preparation and Lysis
steps.instruction: Process the frozen human lung tissue to initiate nuclei isolation.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve human lung sample from -80C or LN2 storage and cut a ~5-7 3 mm piece; keep on dry ice until ready.
Place sample on a small plastic weighing boat on ice and allow to thaw almost completely (~30-60 sec).
Inject ~1 ml of Lysis buffer into the tissue using a 3 ml syringe and 30G needle, moving the needle to distribute the solution evenly ('inflate' the tissue).
Chop tissue into ~1.5-2.0 mm pieces using scissors (~1 min).
Transfer chopped tissue and solution into a C tube and add the remaining lysis buffer to reach a final volume of 2 ml.
Close the C tube, invert to ensure all pieces are at the base, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Mechanical Dissociation
steps.instruction: Dissociate the tissue using a MACS Tissue Dissociator.

substeps.instruction: Place C tube on MACS Tissue Dissociator and run the m_lung_01 program.
Run the m_lung_02 program for 20 sec.
Immediately place the tube on ice.
Briefly spin the tube in a swinging bucket rotor centrifuge (~30 sec, at 4C) to reduce foam.

steps.title: Filtration and Quality Control
steps.instruction: Filter the lysate and verify nuclei quality.

substeps.instruction: Set a 30 um filter on top of a 15 ml polypropylene tube (on ice).
Transfer lysis buffer and remaining lung tissue pieces onto the filter using a wide bore tip.
Rinse the filter with 4 ml of Wash buffer.
Remove the filter, close the tube, mix by inverting, and keep on ice.
Take a 20 ul aliquot for counting using AO/PI solution on a Nexcellom K2 Cellometer; verify that no AO-positive cells are present and PI-positive nuclei are uniformly round or oval.
Add 2 ul of DAPI (5 mg/ml stock) per 1 ml of solution (~12 ul total).
Mix and incubate on ice for 5 min.

steps.title: Cell Sorting
steps.instruction: Sort nuclei using a flow cytometer.

substeps.instruction: Ensure UV laser is on and use a 450/50 filter for DAPI.
Gate on DAPI+ cells on log scale, then switch to linear and gate on G0/G1 and G2/M events, excluding subG0 events and doublets.
Optional: Use SYTO RNA Select Dye (Blue 488 nm laser, 530/50 filter) to identify nuclei containing RNA.

steps.title: Post-Sort Processing
steps.instruction: Choose one of the following options for downstream processing:

substeps.instruction: Option A: Sort 10K events into RT mix, adjust volume to 90 ul with H2O, add RT enzyme, and proceed to 10x Chromium emulsion generation.
Option B: Sort nuclei into 200 ul of Capture buffer in protein lo-bind 1.5 ml tubes and keep on ice.
Option B (cont.): Pellet nuclei using a swinging bucket rotor centrifuge at 300 rcf for 5 min at 4C.
Option B (cont.): Remove supernatant and add Resuspension buffer to obtain 1000 nuclei/ul (adjusting for 20% loss during sorting/centrifugation).
Option B (cont.): Let sit on ice for 1 min, gently resuspend the pellet, filter through a 30 um filter if necessary, count nuclei, adjust concentration, and proceed with 10x Chromium.
